The denominator is $-1+4\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-1-4\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-1-4\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\text{i}}{-1+4\text{i}} & =\frac{4\text{i}}{-1+4\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-1-4\text{i}}{-1-4\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-4\text{i}-16{\text{i}}^{2}}{(-1)^{2}-(4\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-4\text{i}-16(-1)}{1-(-16)} \\  & =\frac{16-4\text{i}}{17}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\frac{16-4\text{i}}{17}=(\frac{16}{17})+(-\frac{4}{17})\,\text{i}
$$
